hints: Focus on what really moves in this reaction, a proton from HCl to the lone pair on ammonia, not electrons to chlorine.
Compare the electron domains around nitrogen in $\text{NH}_3$ with three bonds plus one lone pair, to $\text{NH}_4^+$ with four bonds and no lone pair.
Think how losing the lone pair changes the shape from pyramidal to tetrahedral, and what that means for bond angle, symmetry and hybridisation.
walkthrough:
**Spot the real reaction type**

This is an acid-base proton transfer, not redox. Ammonia uses its lone pair to accept $\text{H}^+$.

$$\text{NH}_3 + \text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{NH}_4^+ + \text{Cl}^-$$

**Compare shapes and bond angles**

In $\text{NH}_3$ nitrogen has 4 electron domains, 3 bonding plus 1 lone pair, so it is trigonal pyramidal with $\text{H-N-H} \approx 107^{\circ}$.

In $\text{NH}_4^+$ nitrogen still has 4 electron domains, but now all 4 are bonding, so it is tetrahedral with $\text{H-N-H} = 109.5^{\circ}$. The angle increases.

**Check hybridisation of nitrogen**

Both cases have 4 electron domains arranged tetrahedrally, so nitrogen is $sp^3$ hybridised in both.

$$\text{NH}_3: sp^3 \text{ (3 } \sigma \text{ bonds + lone pair)} \rightarrow \text{NH}_4^+: sp^3 \text{ (4 } \sigma \text{ bonds)}$$ The new N-H bond is a dative covalent bond, but the orbital picture does not change.

**Check polarity and electron transfer**

$\text{NH}_3$ is unsymmetrical and polar, so it has a dipole moment. $\text{NH}_4^+$ is perfectly tetrahedral and symmetrical, so its bond dipoles cancel and its dipole moment is zero. There is no electron transfer to chlorine, only $\text{H}^+$ transfer to nitrogen.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{NH}_3$ is pyramidal and polar with a permanent dipole. $\text{NH}_4^+$ is tetrahedral and symmetrical, so the four N-H bond dipoles cancel and the overall dipole moment is zero, which is smaller, not greater.
options.B: Incorrect. The lone pair in $\text{NH}_3$ repels strongly and squeezes the angle to about 107 degrees. When it becomes a bonding pair in $\text{NH}_4^+$, repulsion is less and the angle opens to the tetrahedral 109.5 degrees, so the angle increases.
options.C: Correct. Nitrogen has 4 electron domains in both species, so it stays $sp^3$ hybridised. The only change is that the lone pair in $\text{NH}_3$ becomes the fourth dative N-H bond in $\text{NH}_4^+$.
options.D: Incorrect. This is a common redox trap. No electrons are transferred from N to Cl. Chlorine stays as $\text{Cl}^-$ and nitrogen donates its lone pair to $\text{H}^+$ to form a dative covalent bond. It is proton transfer, not electron transfer.
